name: AI Deep Dive — PLTR — 2026-05-02
rationale: Palantir is experiencing a massive growth inflection driven by its Artificial Intelligence Platform (AIP). Trailing revenue grew 70% to $4.48B, and the company has achieved structural profitability with a 36.3% TTM net margin, yielding an exceptional 102.18 Rule of 40 score. However, this hypergrowth is entirely priced in at the current valuation (228.7x trailing P/E, 77.2x forward P/E). Even applying generous hypergrowth assumptions (34% CAGR) and a premium 50x exit multiple, our base case fair value sits at $122.92. The stock trades at a ~15% premium to this base case, making it slightly overvalued despite the phenomenal underlying business execution. SELL.

bear.rationale: Growth decelerates sharply to 25% as the initial AIP 'bootcamp' surge matures and commercial sales cycles lengthen. Net margin compresses to 30% due to increased sales and marketing expenses needed to acquire non-government customers. The exit P/E compresses to 40x. Stock-based compensation causes 2% annual dilution. The 1.1x quality multiplier reflects high switching costs within their government and defense contracts.
risks: Government spending contracts normalize post-geopolitical peaks
Commercial AIP adoption stalls as enterprises struggle to demonstrate ROI

base.rationale: Hypergrowth exception applied: initial analyst consensus of ~62% for Y1 smoothly decelerates to derive a 34% 5-year CAGR. Net margin remains exceptional at 36%, reflecting massive operating leverage on software scaling. The exit P/E remains elevated at 50x to account for Palantir's unique position as an AI platform for defense and critical enterprise. A quality multiplier of 1.2x is applied due to their near-monopoly in classified US government data ontology.
risks: Valuation premium vulnerable to any quarter where growth dips below 30%
Commercial sector competition from Microsoft (Fabric) and Databricks

bull.rationale: Catalyst: Palantir AIP becomes the definitive standard OS for corporate AI, penetrating the Global 2000 far faster than anticipated. Growth sustains a massive 42% CAGR over 5 years. Software operating leverage drives net margins up to an unprecedented 42%. The market awards a 65x exit P/E to reflect absolute dominance in the enterprise AI space. The 1.3x quality multiplier reflects a dual monopoly in Western defense intelligence and corporate AI orchestration.
risks: Extreme multiple (65x exit) assumes perfect execution and zero macro disruption

analyticsLog.marginAnchor: TTM 36.31% used. Palantir has structurally inflected from heavy losses (-19.6% two years ago) to massive profitability. Base case holds margin flat at 36% as a conservative estimate of steady-state SaaS operating leverage.
analyticsLog.growthDerivation: Hypergrowth exception applied. Analyst Y1 revenue implies 62.6% growth ($7.27B vs $4.47B TTM). Y2 implies 43.1%. Projecting a natural deceleration path (30%, 20%, 15% in years 3-5) yields a 5-yr CAGR of ~34%. Base case growth set to 34%.

name: AI Deep Dive — PLTR — 2026-07-02
rationale: Palantir remains a genuinely profitable, structurally-moated AI/data platform (82%+ gross margin, 43.7% TTM net margin, government + commercial lock-in via Gotham/Foundry ontology), but the market is pricing it at 147-154x trailing earnings — a multiple a 5-year DCF cannot justify carrying forward. A refreshed, independently-derived model puts fair value at $147.06 against $130.96, a modest 12.3% upside — HOLD, not the SELL the 60-day-stale prior model showed, and not the outright buy that recent bullish news coverage implied either.

aiThesis.rationale: Palantir has continued its transformation into a genuinely profitable software platform: TTM net margin of 43.7% (up from 36.3% a year ago, -19.6% four years ago), 82%+ gross margins, and FY2026 analyst revenue guidance of $7.72B (+72.5% YoY). The structural moat is real — Gotham and Foundry create deep government/enterprise ontology lock-in with high switching costs, which justifies a qualityMultiplier above 1.1 in the base and bull cases. However, the market is currently pricing PLTR at 147-154x trailing earnings, a multiple no reasonable 5-year DCF exit assumption can sustain — even the bull case caps exit P/E at 65x. A refreshed valuation (independently re-derived, not anchored to the 60-day-stale prior SELL call or to today's price) lands at a weighted fair value of $147.06 against a $130.96 price: 12.3% upside, HOLD. This sits between the stale DCF's prior SELL and the recent Grok/Gemini news sweeps' bullish 'INITIATE NOW' calls — the fundamentals genuinely improved and justify a higher fair value than the prior model found, but the current price already captures most of that improvement. Not a compelling initiation at today's price; would become one on a pullback toward the mid-$110s (base-case entry with margin of safety) or on evidence that Y3-Y5 growth decelerates slower than the modeled path.

analyticsLog.shareCountMethod: shares_diluted (2,296,071,334 shares — direct from raw metrics)
analyticsLog.marginAnchor: TTM (43.67%) — margin has expanded every year for 4 consecutive years (-19.6% -> 9.4% -> 16.1% -> 36.3% -> 43.67% TTM), qualifies as trending per anchoring rule. Base case set to 44% (near TTM, no material deviation). Bear deviates to 27% (>5pp below TTM) to reflect competitive/execution risk from hyperscaler-native AI agent platforms and government spending pressure compressing margins back toward sector-typical levels; bull expands modestly to 47% on continued operating leverage.
analyticsLog.growthDerivation: Analyst consensus: FY2026 (Y1) revenue $7.72B avg (+72.5% vs TTM $4.48B), FY2027 (Y2) $11.20B avg (+45.1% YoY). Hypergrowth exception applied (Y1 consensus >40%): growth increment (72.5% -> 45.1%, a 27.4pp drop) halved each subsequent year -> Y3 ~31.4%, Y4 ~24.6%, Y5 ~21.1%. Derived 5yr revenue CAGR from (Y5 rev / TTM rev)^(1/5)-1 = ~37.8%. Base case growthRate set to 36% (close to derived CAGR, slightly conservative). Bear (18%) reflects deceleration overshooting consensus on commercial competition; bull (48%) reflects accelerating commercial AIP adoption beyond backlog trajectory (named catalyst).
analyticsLog.sectorBenchmarkRow: Technology — Software (SaaS): Conservative P/E 20, Median P/E 30, Growth P/E 50+ | Net margin Bear Trough 0%, Typical 15-25%, Best-in-Class 30%+. PLTR's TTM margin (43.7%) already exceeds best-in-class SaaS, so base/bull exitPE anchored at the top of the Growth P/E band (50/65) rather than extrapolating today's 147-154x trailing multiple.
dataQualityFlags: TTM profit_margin (43.67%) initially computed as 0.0 by standardize_metrics.py because raw fetch_financials.py output omits a 'net_income' key for PLTR (only provides profit_margin + pe_ratio) — root-caused and fixed in this session (net_income now derived from profit_margin x revenue when missing); net_income now correctly resolves to ~$1.95B.
Current market multiple (147-154x trailing P/E) is extreme relative to even the bull-case exit P/E (65x) — DCF intentionally does not extrapolate this multiple 5 years forward.
rev_cagr_3yr from historical data reports 0.0 due to a leading zero-padded entry in historical_revenue array — not used as the growth anchor; analyst-consensus-derived CAGR used instead.

Prior exitPE (30/45/60) was slightly more conservative than this run's (35/50/65) — re-derived independently rather than carried forward, landing close but not identical.

priorAnalysisReview.thesisOutcome: Partially played out — price fell 9.1% toward (but did not reach) the prior $96.54 fair value, consistent with the prior SELL direction. However, a full re-derivation with corrected fundamentals data lands at a materially different fair value ($147.06 vs $96.54), driven primarily by the net_income/profit_margin bug fix (prior run likely also affected) and updated analyst consensus.
priorAnalysisReview.fundamentalChanges: Two AI News sweeps (Grok + Gemini, 2026-07-01) both independently rated PLTR 'INITIATE NOW' citing FY2026 revenue guidance raised to $7.66B (71% YoY) and a zero-debt balance sheet — this news read conflicted with the stale DCF's SELL rating, which is what triggered this refresh.

analyticsLog.confidenceBreakdown: 0.65/1.0 — Base 1.0. -0.15 for extreme current market multiple (147-154x) creating wide dispersion between scenarios. -0.10 for reliance on only 2 years of forward analyst estimates (Y3-Y5 are deceleration-modeled, not consensus). -0.10 for government-contract revenue concentration risk (budget/political exposure). +0.10 for genuine trending margin expansion (4 consecutive years) and 82%+ gross margin structural moat (Gotham/Foundry ontology lock-in, high switching costs).
